purpose: Fresh verification cases specified after the first repaired run exposed speculative adjacent matches, before running the stricter acceptance policy.

profiles.name: [VERIFY] Quinn
profiles.need: People abandon my checkout and I can't tell whether the labels make sense. I want to watch a few people try it and learn where they get confused, not just make it prettier.
profiles.offer: I can spot low colour contrast and suggest more readable text sizes on a phone.

profiles.name: [VERIFY] Avery R
profiles.need: My web page looks like a wall of text. Can someone help with typography and a clearer visual hierarchy?
profiles.offer: I run small usability sessions: asking people to try a rough prototype, think aloud and show where they get stuck.

profiles.name: [VERIFY] Jules D
profiles.need: My colleagues cannot open the website I run locally. I want to publish a version they can use through a normal link.
profiles.offer: I can help make a web page easier to scan through type sizes, spacing and visual hierarchy. I don't fix code or set up hosting.

profiles.name: [VERIFY] Kai H
profiles.need: I need help making the small pale-grey text on my mobile form easier to read.
profiles.offer: I can host and deploy a small website and help connect its public address. I don't run usability research.

checks.reason: Observing checkout confusion through user sessions versus explicit usability-session offer.
Text-heavy page hierarchy versus typography/spacing offer.
Let colleagues open a local site via a link versus website hosting/deployment.
Hard-to-read pale phone text versus contrast/text-size help.
Hosting with explicit exclusion of research does not answer usability-research need.
Running usability sessions does not promise deployment.
Self-recommendation remains excluded regardless of relevance.
